items.translatedQuestion: Please tell us about the origin of the name “Guangzhou.”
items.translatedAnswer: During the Eastern Wu period of the Three Kingdoms, the area north of Hepu was designated Guangzhou and administered the commanderies of Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, and others. The name “Guangzhou” dates from this designation.

items.translatedQuestion: Please describe the climate of Guangdong.
items.translatedAnswer: Guangdong lies in the subtropical zone and has a mild climate with abundant rainfall. Its average annual temperature is about 22.3°C, and its average annual precipitation is 1,700 millimeters.

items.translatedQuestion: Please talk about the history of Guangdong during the Pre-Qin period.
items.translatedAnswer: During the Pre-Qin period, this area was inhabited by the Nanyue people, one of the Baiyue peoples. In 219 BCE, Qin Shi Huang unified Lingnan and established the three commanderies of Guilin, Xiang, and Nanhai. Present-day Guangzhou was the seat of Nanhai Commandery.

items.translatedQuestion: What do you know about the Kingdom of Nanyue?
items.translatedAnswer: In the early Western Han period, Zhao Tuo, a former Qin general, established the first local regime in Lingnan, the Kingdom of Nanyue, in what is now Guangdong. It promoted integration between the Han and Yue peoples and accelerated social, economic, and cultural development in Lingnan.

items.translatedQuestion: What are the four famous gardens of Guangdong Province?
items.translatedAnswer: Qinghui Garden, Keyuan Garden, Yuyin Shanfang Garden, and Liang Garden are the four most famous gardens in Guangdong and are representative of Lingnan gardens.

items.translatedQuestion: What are China’s four famous embroidery traditions?
items.translatedAnswer: Guangdong embroidery, together with Suzhou embroidery, Hunan embroidery, and Sichuan embroidery, is known as one of China’s “Four Great Embroideries.”

items.translatedQuestion: Can you introduce the three major regional communities in Guangdong?
items.translatedAnswer: They are the Guangfu, Chaoshan, and Hakka communities, corresponding respectively to Guangfu, Chaoshan, and Hakka culture and embodying the essence of Lingnan culture. The Guangfu community formed earliest among the three and is concentrated mainly in the Pearl River Delta and in some counties and cities in central and western Guangdong.

items.translatedQuestion: What is the most apparent feature that distinguishes the three communities?
items.translatedAnswer: Their dialects: “Baihua,” based on the Guangzhou dialect; Hakka, based on the Meixian dialect; and Chaoshan, based on the Shantou dialect.

items.translatedQuestion: Cantonese cuisine is one of China’s four major regional cuisines. Can you introduce the three main styles of cuisine in Guangdong?
items.translatedAnswer: As the saying goes, “The best food is in Guangdong.” Cantonese cuisine mainly comprises Guangzhou, Chaozhou, and Dongjiang styles. Guangzhou cuisine is representative of Cantonese cuisine; its dishes are light, fresh, tender, smooth, and crisp, with great attention to color, aroma, flavor, and presentation. Chaozhou cuisine is known for seafood, especially its soups. Dongjiang cuisine, also known as Hakka cuisine, features many meat dishes, uses generous amounts of oil, and tends to be somewhat salty; clay-pot dishes are a specialty.

items.translatedQuestion: Architecture in Guangdong, as a vehicle of Lingnan culture, has a distinctive style. Can you name some of the province’s unique vernacular buildings?
items.translatedAnswer: Examples include distinctive Lingnan residences such as Xiguan mansions, arcaded buildings, and Hakka walled compounds; ceremonial buildings such as the Nanhai God Temple, Foshan Ancestral Temple, Chen Clan Ancestral Hall, and Panyu Academy; the Kaiping Diaolou, a World Heritage property; and defensive structures such as Xinhui Yamen Fort and Guangzhou’s Zhenhai Tower. All display the characteristics of Lingnan architecture.

items.translatedQuestion: Please explain the origin of the name of Kaiyuan Temple in Chaozhou, Guangdong.
items.translatedAnswer: According to historical records, Kaiyuan Temple was originally called Lifeng Temple and was founded around the Sui-Tang transition. In the 26th year of the Kaiyuan era (738 CE), Emperor Xuanzong of Tang ordered each of the country’s 81 prefectures and counties to select a major temple and name it after his era name, Kaiyuan, in celebration of his birthday. Chaozhou accordingly renamed Lifeng Temple Kaiyuan Temple.

items.translatedQuestion: What can we learn from the jade seals excavated from the tomb of the King of Nanyue?
items.translatedAnswer: Of the nine jade seals, three were found on the occupant’s body in the main coffin chamber. They were inscribed “Zhao Mo,” “Crown Prince,” and “Seal of the Emperor,” respectively, and provide physical evidence that Zhao Mo usurped the title of emperor.

items.translatedQuestion: Please introduce the Zidong pleasure boat in Baomo Garden, Panyu, Guangdong.
items.translatedAnswer: The Zidong pleasure boat is characteristic of the Pearl River Delta. It is lavishly decorated, with dining tables at the bow and a kitchen at the stern. Such boats were most popular during the Ming and Qing dynasties. Originally used as pleasure craft by wealthy families, they later developed into teahouses on the water.

items.translatedQuestion: What is the meaning of the stone relief titled “Noble Rank, Official Emoluments, and Enfeoffment as a Marquis” on the wall behind the stone drum to the right of the entrance to the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall in Guangzhou?
items.translatedAnswer: The relief is an allegorical image showing a bird, a deer, a bee, and a monkey. Their Chinese names are homophones for “noble rank,” “official emoluments,” “enfeoffment,” and “marquis,” respectively, together conveying the wish that members of the Chen family would receive noble titles and lucrative official appointments.

items.translatedQuestion: Where do Guangdong’s ethnic minorities mainly live, and can you tell us about their customs?
items.translatedAnswer: Guangdong’s ethnic minorities are concentrated mainly in areas such as Liannan and Ruyuan. Their distinctive customs include the Yao people’s Getang singing gatherings and cloth-bag wooden-lion tradition; the Zhuang people’s April Eighth festival and Ox King’s Birthday; and the She people’s Second Day of the Second Month and Third Day of the Third Month festivals.

items.translatedQuestion: What kind of regime was the Kingdom of Nanyue? How many generations of rulers did it have, how long did it last, and in what year and under which dynasty did it come under central rule?
items.translatedAnswer: The Kingdom of Nanyue was a local regime in southern China during the Western Han period. It had five successive generations of rulers and lasted 93 years. In the sixth year of Emperor Wu’s Yuanding era (111 BCE), it came under the Western Han.

items.translatedQuestion: What are some of the well-known forest parks in Guangdong Province?
items.translatedAnswer: They include Liuxi River Forest Park, Xiqiao Mountain Forest Park, Nanling National Forest Park, Nankunshan Forest Park, and Shimen Forest Bathing Area, among other rich forest-tourism resources…

items.translatedQuestion: Please tell us what you know about Guangdong carving and its well-known traditional crafts.
items.translatedAnswer: Guangdong carving, represented by ivory, jade, and wood carving, is delicate and highly accomplished, with an exceptionally high artistic standard. The province’s distinctive crafts include Duan inkstones from Zhaoqing, paper-cutting and lion-head making in Foshan, palm-leaf crafts in Xinhui, and lacquerware in Yangjiang. These crafts all have long histories and a high level of artistry.

items.translatedQuestion: Why is the architectural decorative art of the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall said to have a strong local Guangdong character?
items.translatedAnswer: From top to bottom and inside and out, its columns, eaves, ridges, steps, doors, windows, and other features are adorned with woodcarvings, brick and stone carvings, ceramic and gray-plaster sculptures, ironwork, and other crafts. These works are not only decorative; they also draw on historical and mythological stories, while motifs composed of flowers, birds, insects, fish, and other creatures carry symbolic meanings. For example, peonies symbolize wealth and prosperity, paired lotus flowers symbolize marital devotion, and lions symbolize power and dignity.

items.translatedQuestion: Why is the Ancestral Temple in Foshan known as the “Palace of Oriental Folk Art”?
items.translatedAnswer: Its ridges, eaves, walls, and interior are decorated with ceramic and gray-plaster sculptures, brick carvings, woodcarvings, and other works depicting traditional Chinese folk stories and myths. These decorations are finely crafted, with lifelike figures, and are precious examples of ancient Chinese art. For this reason, the Ancestral Temple is known as the “Palace of Oriental Folk Art.”

items.translatedQuestion: Why is Huineng, together with Confucius and Laozi, called one of the “Three Great Sages of the East” and regarded by European scholars as one of the world’s ten great thinkers?
items.translatedAnswer: Huineng’s doctrine of sudden enlightenment had a profound impact on Buddhism, making Chan the mainstream school of Chinese Buddhism, and also greatly influenced Chinese philosophical thought. For this reason, he is regarded alongside Confucius and Laozi as one of the “Three Great Sages of the East”; European scholars have also called him one of the world’s ten great thinkers.

items.translatedQuestion: Can you list the types of carving and other crafted works used to decorate the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall?
items.translatedAnswer: Craftworks found throughout the hall include stone carvings, brick carvings, gray-plaster sculptures, ceramic sculptures, woodcarvings, and iron-cast components.

items.translatedQuestion: What does “Xiguan mansion” mean in Guangzhou?
items.translatedAnswer: In the lanes around Shangxiajiu Road, there are residences with distinctive forms and structures. Formerly homes of wealthy merchants, they are known as Xiguan mansions. These houses are large and sturdy, and both their interiors and exteriors are decorated with woodcarvings, stone carvings, ceramic sculptures, and gray-plaster sculptures. They were among Guangzhou’s most representative residential buildings of their time.

items.translatedQuestion: What are the four most famous temples in Guangdong Province?
items.translatedAnswer: They are Kaiyuan Temple in Chaozhou, Nanhua Temple in Shaoguan, Qingyun Temple in Zhaoqing, and Guangxiao Temple in Guangzhou.

items.translatedQuestion: Five of the ten generals of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army graduated from the Whampoa Military Academy. Can you name them?
items.translatedAnswer: They are Ye Jianying, Nie Rongzhen, Chen Yi, Xu Xiangqian, and Lin Biao.

items.translatedQuestion: Why are the stone drums on either side of the main entrance regarded as a symbol of the Chen family’s status?
items.translatedAnswer: In feudal China, a family could place a pair of large drums in front of its residence only if one of its members had attained at least the jinshi degree in the imperial examinations. In the 18th year of the Guangxu reign (1893), the year before the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall was completed, Chen Botao of the Chen family attained the rank of tanhua, the third-place laureate in the highest imperial examination. The stone drums were therefore installed in his honor.

items.translatedQuestion: What are “cliff inscriptions”?
items.translatedAnswer: “Cliff inscriptions” are images and writing carved into relatively flat surfaces of natural rock, including records of achievements and events. They are usually created jointly by literati calligraphers and stonemasons.

items.translatedQuestion: What are the four most famous mountains in the Lingnan region?
items.translatedAnswer: Danxia Mountain, Luofu Mountain, Xiqiao Mountain, and Dinghu Mountain are the four most famous mountains in the Lingnan region.

items.translatedQuestion: In July 2026, the Publicity Department of the CPC Guangdong Provincial Committee, the Guangdong Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism, and the Guangdong Provincial Department of Education jointly issued guidelines for premium study-tour themes and routes in Guangdong under two categories: humanities and science and technology. What specific themes are included in the science and technology category?
items.translatedAnswer: The science and technology category of the Guangdong premium study-tour themes comprises four themes: AI-powered manufacturing, electronic information, biomedicine, and digital cultural and creative industries.

items.translatedQuestion: In July 2026, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism issued the 15th Five-Year Plan for Building China into a Tourism Power. What five major missions does it set out for accelerating this effort over the next five years?
items.translatedAnswer: The five missions are to enable tourism to better serve people’s aspirations for a better life; promote economic development; build a spiritual home; showcase China’s image; and foster mutual learning among civilizations.

items.translatedQuestion: Where was the main event for 2026 China Tourism Day, held on May 19, and what was this year’s theme?
items.translatedAnswer: The main event for 2026 China Tourism Day was held in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province. This year’s theme was “Enjoy Quality Travel and Explore Beautiful Landscapes Together.”

items.translatedQuestion: On July 25, 2026, at the 48th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, which Chinese nomination was inscribed on the World Heritage List? How many World Heritage properties does China have in total as a result?
items.translatedAnswer: At the 48th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, China’s nomination “Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites” was inscribed on the World Heritage List, bringing the country’s total to 61 properties.

items.translatedQuestion: On December 11, 2025, which Chinese element was transferred to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity? What is the resulting total number of Chinese elements on UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage lists and register?
items.translatedAnswer: Hezhen Yimakan storytelling was transferred to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, bringing the total number of Chinese elements on UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage lists and register to 45.

items.translatedQuestion: Starting November 5, 2025, which five ports in Guangdong Province did the National Immigration Administration add to the 240-hour visa-free transit policy?
items.translatedAnswer: The five ports are Guangzhou Pazhou Passenger Port, Hengqin Port, Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Port, Zhongshan Port, and the West Kowloon Station port of the Guangzhou–Shenzhen–Hong Kong Express Rail Link.

items.translatedQuestion: From March to April 2025, the American online influencer known as “Hyperthyroidism Bro” explored and documented authentic Chinese life and scenery from a more independent, immersive, personal perspective, becoming an enthusiastic grassroots ambassador for China’s image. Which cities did he visit on his trip to China?
items.translatedAnswer: Shanghai, Beijing, Dengfeng in Henan (including the Shaolin Temple), Chengdu, Chongqing, Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Changsha.

items.translatedQuestion: In 2025, “China shopping” became a global sensation. What were the “old three” and “new three” on the shopping lists of foreign visitors coming to China?
items.translatedAnswer: The “old three” are silk, tea, and porcelain; the “new three” are small household appliances, drones, and trendy cultural and creative products.

items.translatedQuestion: Starting on May 10, 2025, which league became a phenomenal cultural-tourism sensation, propelled by online catchphrases such as “Competition first, friendship fourteenth” and “the Thirteen Taibao,” as well as highly entertaining matches?
items.translatedAnswer: The Jiangsu City Football League, commonly known as the “Su Super League.”

items.translatedQuestion: During China Brand Day in May 2026, which Guangdong brands were included among the first 30 recommended “Travel with Brands” experience destinations?
items.translatedAnswer: DJI and Fengyi Smart Logistics, both based in Shenzhen.
